title: Earle Warren replaces Roberts; New York union rule and Clifton Glover
summary: Earle Warren replaced Caughey Roberts, and Clayton recalls a union rule requiring local men like Clifton Glover to direct the band.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well when does, when does Earl Warren come into the, when does he, he comes into the band fairly early doesn't he?
pretty early. We had to send Coughy back, that's right, yes. Coughy didn't quite, didn't quite make it. Not like Earl did. He wasn't quite, he wasn't a lead man that Earl is. And he wasn't soloist.
Earl has never been a hell of a soloist, but he was better than- Coughy . He wasn't a bad soloist, I don't mean that. I don't mean he was never like Johnny Hodges.
No, but he could take care of this, now did Earl take care of the conducting?
Or did you just dispense with that?

I think we just, we did, yes. All of us had to learn parts. And then sometimes, now here's a funny thing. You met Clifton Glover today. Clifton Glover has always been in the New York Union, twenty two years. But at that time, no he must have been in there before, longer than twenty, he's probably been an executive or something that long.
But at one time there was a rule in New York, you had to have a certain amount of local men on hand even if they didn't play. And then

sometimes they would play the show. And I remember Cliff Clever being the director of Basie's band one time in the Apollo Theater. And he was scared stiff. And that's why he always likes me, Earl Warren and Jo Jones because we said, look, don't worry, all you have to do is bring the stick down and we got it.

So he's a very young cat. So he would bring the stick down and we would shoot on with it. You know, that's all he had to do. The same Cliff. And he talks about that all the time. How he used to be surprised how we could swing and the New York bands didn't have the same feeling. You know they were good bands, but ....
